fact: The NCC consultation paper says the National Telecommunications Policy 2000 is the subsisting sector policy, in force for twenty-five years and now under review.

The paper, dated 9 February 2026, is the first step toward a First Draft of a National Telecommunications Policy 2026 to replace the 2000 policy, with a Final Draft to follow further consultation and statutory approval and validation.

The Minister of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy set up a Ministerial Steering Committee and a Ministerial Technical Committee to review the policy, and an Implementation Committee ran the policy impact analysis; the consultation is required by s.24(1) of the Nigerian Communications Act 2003.
The paper describes the 2000 policy as still subsisting after twenty-five years, and states no end date for it; Chapter 16 provides review only 'from time to time'.

The paper reproduces Chapter 16 of the 2000 policy as three implementation instruments (machinery, a national forum, annual reports) and proposes to add a detailed implementation matrix, milestones, dependencies and responsible parties, so none exists in the current text.
The NCC published fifteen policy proposals for rewriting the 2000 policy and invited stakeholder comments by 20 March 2026.

The Minister of Communications' preface of May 2000 presents the National Policy on Telecommunications as the policy approved by the President and launched in October 1999, revised by a steering committee under the National Council on Privatization.
The full policy text, with seventeen chapters, was published in May 2000 under the Ministry of Communications.
The policy assigns policy formulation to the Ministry of Communications and regulation to the Nigerian Communications Commission, and sets up a National Frequency Management Council in the Ministry.
